questions.q: What are natural resources, and how are they classified?
answer: Natural resources are the useful materials we obtain from nature — land, soil, water, air, minerals, forests, wildlife and energy — and they form the basis of all human activity.

answer.text: Renewable resources can be replenished within a reasonable time, such as solar energy, wind, water, forests and soil. Non-renewable resources are limited and take millions of years to form, such as coal, petroleum, natural gas and minerals.
Biotic resources come from living things, while abiotic resources come from non-living things.
Actual resources are those being used now, while potential resources exist but are not yet used. Their distribution across the world and within India is very uneven.

questions.q: Distinguish between conventional and non-conventional energy sources, and explain why India is promoting renewable energy.

answer.text: These are the traditional, mostly non-renewable sources — the fossil fuels coal, petroleum and natural gas, along with nuclear energy. They are limited and their burning pollutes the environment.
These are the newer, renewable sources — solar, wind, hydro, tidal, geothermal and biomass energy — which are clean and do not run out.

Because fossil fuels are limited and cause pollution and climate change, India is increasingly promoting renewable energy, especially solar and wind, to secure a clean and lasting supply of power and to reduce its dependence on imported fuels.
